title: The Rose of Versailles
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Oscar François de Jarjayes, a noblewoman raised as a son by her father, becomes commander of Marie Antoinette's palace guard and, with her servant André, witnesses the luxury and intrigue of Louis XVI's court (Udon blurb via AniList and MU). Court rivalries, poisonings, arson and the Diamond Necklace affair foreshadow the queen's fall, while the orphan Rosalie's poverty awakens Oscar's sympathy for the common people as the French Revolution approaches (Solrad review; MU French Revolution, Execution).
life_message: Conscience and love can lead a person to break with rank and privilege to stand with the suffering, even at great cost.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Aristocratic honor and swordplay present but the story sides with justice over rank (review).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Oscar's duty as guard commander against the people's freedom; tension unresolved (MU blurb; review).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Father's will shapes Oscar, but her loyalty widens to the common people (review).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Aristocratic cruelty to the poor is critiqued (review; AniList Class Struggle).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Inherited monarchy and gender roles questioned (AniList Gender Bending; review).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Oscar's freedom to be herself balanced against poverty's survival stakes (review).

folkways.japan: A landmark 1970s shojo work that used a European setting to explore gender and class questions current in Japan; Takarazuka Revue staging is part of its context (to verify).

delivery.evidence: Reviewer says it refuses a 'benign fantasy' of royalty and stresses class themes through Rosalie and Oscar.

personified.ideology: Conscience and gender freedom against inherited rank

delivery.note: Monarchy is critiqued, but the queen is given a human, tragic portrait rather than a caricature (review; MU Tragic Protagonist).

winners_losers: History sides with the revolution; the old court loses, and many sympathetic characters meet tragic ends. Sympathy is with conscience, the poor and Oscar's chosen identity.
